lines.t: Stop.
A sound.
You didn't decide to hear it.
It arrived already heard.
Breathe in.
That air was outside you a second ago.
Now it isn't.
Where did it cross over?
Something you ate last week is your hand now.
It was an apple. Or rice. Or a fish.
When exactly did it become you?
Don't answer. Look for the moment.
Wait here for the next thought.
It'll come.
Watch where it comes from.
You can't see where it comes from.
Notice you also didn't make it.
Something went wrong today.
It happened once.
The telling has happened forty times.
Which one is hurting you?
Someone cuts in front of you.
Heat.
It came before the thought about it.
Watch the thought arrive second.
There's an itch somewhere. Find it.
Now — is the itch being felt,
or are you feeling it?
Look. Don't decide.
You're waiting for a reply.
Notice the checking.
Notice the small drop each time nothing is there.
That drop is known.
By what?
Look at your hands.
They were smaller once.
Completely different material.
Something didn't change.
What?
Anger comes.
You didn't send for it.
Anger is known.
Is the knowing angry?
Nothing is happening.
Notice the pressure to make something happen.
That pressure is known too.
A dog flinches before it thinks about flinching.
So did you, this morning.
Same flinch. Older than both of you.
Something good happened. Lightness.
It will pass. You know it will pass.
Watch it being known —
the same way the heavy things are known.
Same room. No difference.
You've been looking.
Who has been looking?
Don't name it.
Stay there a moment longer than is comfortable.
Traffic outside. It's been going the whole time.
You just started listening.
Where was it before that?
Your own voice, recorded, sounds like a stranger's.
But the one you hear when you talk — that one sounds like you.
Which is the real one?
A clock ticking in the next room.
It was always there.
You weren't.
What changed?
Someone says your name across a crowded room.
You turned before you decided to.
What turned?
Silence. Actually listen to it.
It isn't nothing.
It's heard the same way the traffic is heard.
Two sounds at once — a voice, a fan.
You didn't choose which one to notice first.
Something did.
What?
A song comes on and the whole room feels different.
Notice the feeling changed.
Don't look for the reason yet.
Just the change.
One color catches your eye before you've named it.
The naming comes a half-second later.
What did the catching?
Stare at one word until it stops looking like a word.
It becomes shapes.
It was always shapes.
What put the meaning there?
You catch your reflection in a dark window, not expecting it.
For half a second, before recognition, something was seen.
What was seen?
Something moves at the edge of your vision.
You turned toward it before deciding to look.
What turned?
A dark room. Shapes arrive before you know what they are.
For a moment, seeing happens without a story about what's seen.
Then the story starts.
You can tell someone's upset from across a room, before a word is said.
How do you know that?
Don't answer. Look for the knowing itself.
Close your eyes.
Images still arrive.
You're not making them on purpose.
Who's watching them, then?
A photo of you as a child. Different face, different body.
You still call it "me."
What's the "me" that didn't change?
Feel the fabric on your skin right now.
It's been there the whole time.
You just noticed.
What else is like that?
Walk into a warmer or colder room.
The skin knows before you think "it's warmer in here."
Thinking comes late to almost everything.
A hand on your shoulder, and you know whose it is before you turn.
How?
Don't answer yet. Look at the knowing.
You touch something hot.
The hand pulls back before the thought "that hurts" arrives.
Something moved faster than thinking.
Sun on your skin.
Warmth arriving from ninety-three million miles away.
Where does it stop being the sun's and start being felt as yours?
Cold water over your hands.
Notice the cold arrives before the word "cold."
The word is always describing something already over.
Someone touches your hair without asking.
The flinch happens first.
The reason for the flinch, second.
Watch the order.
You've been sitting the same way a while. Find the discomfort.
Is the discomfort being felt,
or are you feeling it?
Look. Don't decide.
Different spot this time. Find the itch.
Before you scratch — is it asking to be scratched,
or is that just what happens next?
A mosquito bite from three days ago still wants attention.
The wanting is known.
You didn't manufacture the wanting.
Bread baking somewhere.
A memory arrives before you asked for one.
Whose memory got there first?
A smell you can't place.
You know it means something before you know what.
The meaning is late again.
The smell before rain arrives before the rain does.
The body already knows what's coming.
It didn't check the sky.
A stranger passes wearing a scent someone once wore.
For one second you're somewhere else entirely.
Who bought that ticket?
Something's burning in the kitchen.
You're up and moving before you decided to be.
The alarm went off in the body first.
Your home has a smell.
You can't smell it anymore.
Everyone else can.
What else are you this used to?
Coffee, brewing.
Notice something in you wake up before the first sip.
The cup hasn't done anything yet.
First bite of something good.
"This is good" arrives after the tasting, not with it.
What was there in between?
Something bitter touches your tongue.
The whole face reacts before you approve the reaction.
Nobody asked your permission.
Nervous, and there's a metal taste in your mouth.
The body has opinions it never mentioned to you.
Where does it keep them?
The same dish, cooked the same way, tastes different today.
Did the food change,
or did you?
Real thirst, then water.
The relief is known before "I feel better" is thought.
Thinking is always the last to arrive at the party.
Someone yawns near you.
You're yawning too, now.
You didn't vote on that.
A scare — the breath goes short and fast.
That happened before you decided to be afraid.
The body voted first.
Hold your breath for a moment.
Notice something counting, keeping track of how long.
You didn't start the count on purpose.
A long day ends. A sigh happens on its own.
You didn't schedule it.
It just came out.
Real laughter takes the breath and does what it wants with it.
For a second you're not steering anything.
Who usually is?
Something startles you.
The heart speeds up before the thought "I'm scared" forms.
It didn't wait for the thought's permission.
A quiet moment. The heart slows on its own.
You didn't order that either.
Who's running this?
Find your pulse. In your wrist, your neck.
It's been going since before you had a name.
When did you start calling it yours?
Two people talking closely, hearts tend to fall into step.
Nobody agreed to that in advance.
It just happens between bodies.
A hunger pang arrives.
The decision to eat comes after.
The pang didn't ask first.
Eating, and then — enough. Something in you says stop.
You didn't calculate that.
Who did?
You're already reaching for water.
The thirst was noticed after the reaching started.
What reached first?
Before speaking in front of people, the mouth goes dry.
Nobody asked the mouth to do that.
It has its own read on the room.
A thought arrives mid-sentence, fully formed.
You didn't build it word by word.
It showed up finished.
Try to stop thinking for ten seconds.
A thought about stopping shows up.
Who sent that one?
An old argument replays in your head, uninvited.
You're not choosing the words this time either.
Who's running it?
A problem you gave up on solves itself in the shower.
You weren't working on it.
Something was.
The same worried thought, for the tenth time today.
A groove worn into something.
What's the groove in?
There's a voice in your head that talks to you all day.
It comments, narrates, argues.
Who is it talking to?
You feel like you're deciding something right now.
Look for the moment of deciding itself.
Or does the decision just arrive, already made?
A song plays in your head, on a loop, uninvited.
You didn't press play.
Find whoever did.
A smell, and a whole afternoon from years ago arrives at once.
You didn't go looking for it.
It came to you.
A name won't come. You give up trying.
An hour later it arrives on its own.
Where was it in between?
A memory from age five. Were you there,
or is this a memory of a photo of being there?
Look closely. It matters less than it seems.
You walk into a room and forget why.
For a second, nothing but the blank.
That blank is known too.
Tell an old story again.
Notice it's slightly different this time — a detail moved.
Which version is the memory?
A face you know well, but the name won't come.
Recognizing and naming are two different things happening.
Which one is closer to you?
A place you've never been feels familiar.
The familiarity arrives before any explanation for it.
The explanation is just a guess, after the fact.
The past isn't happening anywhere right now.
Only this thought about it is.
When did you last check?
A worry about tomorrow, happening today.
It isn't tomorrow yet.
Where exactly is the worry standing?
Think of something you were sure would go wrong.
It didn't.
The worry felt just as real as this one does.
One what-if leads to another, and another.
Nobody's steering this chain.
Who's riding it, then?
You checked the lock. You check it again.
What does the second check actually fix?
Look for the feeling underneath the checking.
Waiting on a result. The mind runs the same loop.
You didn't ask it to.
The loop is known.
By what?
3am. The mind won't stop turning something over.
Ask it to stop.
Watch what happens when it doesn't listen.
You assume you know what they thought of you.
You don't, actually.
Where did the assumption come from?
A scenario that hasn't happened, and your heart is already racing.
The body can't tell imagined from real.
Neither, maybe, can the mind that made it.
Rehearsing a hard conversation before it happens.
You've had it four times already, alone, in your head.
None of those were real.
This worry feels urgent.
The urgency is known too.
Is the knowing in a hurry?
A stranger insults you online.
Heat rises before you've finished reading the sentence.
The reading wasn't even done. Who reacted?
Stuck in traffic. Anger with nowhere to go.
No one caused it on purpose.
Where is the anger supposed to land?
You make a mistake and get angry — at yourself.
Who is angry,
and at whom?
An old resentment, years old, still hot when you touch it.
It didn't need you to keep the fire going.
Or did it?
Someone near you gets angry.
You feel your own heat rise in answer.
It isn't even your argument.
The anger from this morning is gone by evening.
You didn't reason it away.
It just left, the way weather does.
A wave of sadness, no clear reason.
You go looking for a cause to attach it to.
Does it need one?
Crying at a movie, for people who don't exist.
The tears don't check first.
What did they check instead?
Missing someone who is in the next room.
They're twenty feet away.
Distance isn't only measured in feet.
Sadness moves through like weather.
It arrived on its own.
Watch — it'll leave the same way.
A room full of people, and you feel entirely alone.
The room didn't cause that.
Where is it coming from?
A date on the calendar, and an old grief surfaces on its own.
The calendar didn't do that.
Something keeps the date better than you do.
Sadness has a place in the body right now.
Find it. Chest, throat, somewhere else.
Don't name it. Just find it.
You're sad, and also think you shouldn't be.
That's two things happening, not one.
Is the "shouldn't" known the same way the sadness is?
Laughter with a friend, for no real reason.
You didn't earn it or plan it.
It just arrived.
One small good thing happens.
Suddenly the whole day looks different.
The day didn't change.
Something ordinary — a tree, a mug — looks good today, for no reason.
Gratitude shows up before you decided to be grateful.
Where does it keep coming from?
Tension you'd stopped noticing finally lets go.
You didn't release it on command.
It released itself.
A stranger does something small and kind.
Something in you lifts, unearned, unasked for.
Notice how easily it spreads.
Doing nothing in particular, and it's enough.
No reason required.
See how long that lasts before a thought interrupts it.
A waiting room. Nothing to do.
Your hand is already reaching for your phone.
Watch the reach before it gets there.
A long meeting. Your mind is three other places.
You didn't send it there.
It went on its own.
A red light that won't change.
Notice the restlessness, not the light.
What's restless?
A silence in conversation lasts two seconds.
It feels unbearable.
Why does empty air need filling?
A repetitive task. Hands busy, mind gone entirely elsewhere.
The hands don't seem to need it.
Who's doing the task, then?
Boredom, insisting something should be different right now.
Different how?
It never quite says.
A quiet room, and the urge to fill it with sound.
Where does that urge come from?
Not from a decision. Look again.
Boredom, right now, is known.
It didn't have to notice itself.
Is whatever's doing the knowing also bored?
An embarrassing memory from years ago surfaces at 3am.
Nobody summoned it.
It came anyway, uninvited, exact as ever.
You blush before you've decided to feel embarrassed.
Heat in the face, no vote taken.
The face moves faster than the choice does.
A mistake, in front of people.
Some part of you wants to disappear, immediately.
That wanting arrived before any thinking about it did.
You compare how you feel inside to how everyone else looks outside.
You've never once seen their inside.
What are you actually comparing?
A small mistake from days ago still won't let go.
Nobody else remembers it.
What's still holding on, and to what?
You apologize. It's accepted.
The weight stays anyway, a while longer.
What is the weight sitting on?
A buzz in your pocket.
The hand is already moving before you decided to check.
Who moved it?
You pull down to refresh again.
Nothing new. You do it again anyway.
What is that reflex actually asking for?
Mid-conversation, your hand finds the phone in your pocket.
You weren't bored, exactly.
What sent the hand?
A message, marked read, no reply yet.
The mind checks it again, as if checking will change it.
What is it hoping to find this time?
Something beautiful happens, and the first move is to film it.
Notice the moment split in two —
the happening, and the recording of the happening.
Someone else's life, on a screen, looks better than yours.
The comparison ran before you agreed to make it.
Who's comparing?
A phantom buzz. The phone didn't move.
Something in you was expecting it anyway.
What was it expecting?
Scrolling, long after the boredom that started it is gone.
"One more" happens again.
Count how many times "one more" has been true tonight.
You posted something. You check the count.
Then again.
What is being fed by that number?
You put the phone down.
Thirty seconds later, it's back in your hand.
You didn't decide that. Watch the next reach happen.
A line at the store, longer than expected.
Impatience rises on its own.
You didn't invite it in.
Someone steps in ahead of you.
Heat, immediately, before any words are exchanged.
The heat arrived first. The story came after.
Elevator doors closing too slowly.
Your finger presses the button again.
As if that ever changed anything.
Someone ahead of you walks slower than you'd like.
Frustration, aimed at a total stranger.
They don't know. Where does the frustration go?
The bus is late. You check the time.
Then again, thirty seconds later.
Did checking make it arrive any sooner?
"Your flight has been delayed."
A groan happens before the sentence is even finished.
The groan didn't wait for permission.
A crowded train. Small adjustments, made without thinking, to keep your distance.
Nobody's directing this.
Everyone's doing it anyway.
The car ahead is slow to move.
Your hand is on the horn before you've decided anything.
What decided for you?
A task sits undone. You do almost anything else instead.
Look at the resistance itself, not the task.
What is it actually made of?
You make a decision.
Regret arrives before you've finished acting on it.
Which one is really yours?
Dread, before starting something hard.
You start anyway, and the dread was worse than the doing.
It always is. Notice that pattern.
You're doing one thing.
Your mind is running two others at the same time.
Who assigned the extra work?
Washing dishes, thinking of nothing in particular.
The answer to a problem you'd shelved arrives, unasked.
It wasn't found. It showed up.
You finish something hard.
Satisfaction arrives before the thought "I did it."
The thought is just catching up.
You redo something for the fifth time.
It was fine after the second.
Whose standard is this?
Deep in focus, then interrupted.
The jolt happens before you register what interrupted you.
What got jolted?
A blank page. Nothing written yet.
Look at the blank itself, not the pressure to fill it.
The blank isn't the problem.
You check your email "just in case."
In case of what, exactly?
There's rarely an answer. The checking happens anyway.
Someone's talking. You're already forming your reply.
Notice how little of what they said actually landed.
Who was listening?
You finish someone's sentence in your head before they do.
Sometimes you're wrong.
What were you actually listening to?
Someone listens to you fully, no reply forming behind their eyes.
Notice how rare that is.
Notice how good it feels, and why.
You cut someone off mid-sentence, without meaning to.
The urge to speak arrived faster than the manners did.
What was in that much of a hurry?
Silence with someone close feels easy.
The same silence with a stranger feels unbearable.
The silence didn't change.
Someone shares gossip about a person you both know.
Notice something in you leans in, uninvited.
What is it hungry for?
You're complimented.
The deflection happens before the thank-you does.
What couldn't just receive it?
An argument. You already know you're right.
Look at the certainty itself, not the argument.
Where does that certainty come from?
Someone finishes your sentence, and gets it wrong.
A flash of "no, that's not it" arrives instantly.
Faster than you could have reasoned your way there.
A joke lands, and you're laughing before you've fully understood it.
The laugh got there first.
Understanding was just catching up again.
You hear about someone else's success.
A small pang arrives, uninvited, before any kind thought does.
It's known.
By what?
A couple online looks happier than you feel today.
You know almost nothing about their actual life.
What are you comparing yourself to?
A sibling comparison from childhood, still running, decades later.
Nobody's refereeing it anymore.
Why is it still being played?
You want something.
You didn't want it until you saw someone else have it.
Whose want is this?
Someone you compete with fails at something.
Relief arrives, then guilt about the relief.
Both are known, one after the other.
A mirror at the gym, and a body next to yours.
A comparison runs before you agreed to run it.
Who started that race?
A friend shares good news.
There's a two-second delay before real happiness for them arrives.
What happens in those two seconds?
A shared moment turns, without warning, into a competition.
Nobody announced the rules.
Who's keeping score?
Watching someone sleep.
Tenderness arrives without a decision behind it.
Where did it come from?
A stranger's baby laughs nearby.
You're smiling before you know why.
The smile got there first.
You miss a place, not a person.
Can a place miss you back?
Notice the missing is the same shape either way.
You recognize a friend by their walk, from far away.
Their face isn't even clear yet.
What did the recognizing, that fast?
A dog meets you at the door.
Nothing complicated in it. No story, no agenda.
What would it be like if greeting someone was only that?
Holding someone's hand.
For a moment, you can't tell where your hand ends.
Where does it end?
You hope a stranger's day goes well.
Nothing in it benefits you.
What is that caring made of?
An old friend, not seen in years.
Within a minute of talking, no time has passed at all.
What didn't age?
You notice someone watching you.
Your walk changes instantly, without instruction.
Who gave the instruction?
Alone, doing something ordinary, and still performing it a little.
For an audience that isn't there.
Who's it for?
Completely alone in your room.
Still straightening up a little, somehow.
Straightening up for whom?
An unexpected mirror in a store.
Your posture straightens before you decide to.
Who saw you first — the mirror, or something in you?
Typing a text, you re-read it as if you were the other person.
Two readers, one message, and only one of you is real.
Which one is writing it?
You're complimented on something you didn't even try for.
It's harder to accept than praise you worked for.
Why does effort make praise easier to believe?
You choose an outfit differently depending on who you'll see.
Someone who isn't in the room yet is already deciding for you.
Notice that.
A video call camera turns on.
The face changes, automatically, before a word is spoken.
Which face is the one underneath?
You reach for a snack.
You're not hungry.
What reached, then?
You drive a familiar route and arrive with no memory of the drive.
Something was steering.
It wasn't the part of you telling this story now.
Your fingers type a password faster than you could say it out loud.
The hands know something the mind can't quite recite.
Where is that knowledge kept?
You sit down. A sigh comes out.
No thought attached, no story.
Just the sigh, on its own.
The same three apps, checked in the same order, every time.
Nobody wrote this routine down.
Who's following it this precisely?
Brushing your teeth, already planning the rest of the day.
The brushing happens without you.
Who's doing it, if you're somewhere else entirely?
A leg bouncing, or a nail being bitten.
You notice only after minutes of it happening.
Who was doing it before you noticed?
"How are you?"
"Fine" comes out before you've actually checked.
Check now. Is it true?
You catch your hand mid-gesture.
For a second it looks exactly like a parent's hand.
When did that arrive?
An old photo of you.
Different face, different body, entirely different world.
The eyes are the same eyes.
What's behind them that didn't change?
You laugh, and for a second it's exactly your childhood laugh.
Nobody rehearsed that.
It just still fits.
You catch your reflection unexpectedly.
For half a second, you don't register your own age.
What was looking, in that half second?
A scar from years ago. Fully healed now.
The pain is completely gone.
Where did it go?
Someone else points out a gray hair before you'd noticed it yourself.
It had been there a while.
What else is true about you that you haven't looked at yet?
Something your body used to do without effort now takes effort.
The surprise at that is its own thing.
Look at the surprise, not the knee.
Your handwriting isn't what it was at eight years old.
You still call both of them "my handwriting."
What stayed constant enough to earn that "my"?
An old recording of your own voice, years back.
It sounds unfamiliar and completely yours at once.
Both true. Sit with that.
A fear that terrified you as a child does nothing to you now.
Did the fear change,
or did you?
A bird lands on a branch.
No hesitation, no weighing of options.
It just lands.
A plant on a windowsill leans toward the light.
Nobody taught it that.
It just does it.
An ant carries something many times its own size.
No complaint, no story about how hard this is.
Just the carrying.
Waves arrive, and leave, and arrive again.
The same water, or is it?
Notice you're not sure, and it doesn't matter.
A storm passes.
After, everything is completely still.
The stillness was there before the storm too.
Stand under a tree older than your grandparents.
It was here before your family's name existed.
It will likely outlast the name too.
A cat sleeps in a patch of sun for hours.
No guilt about the wasted afternoon.
There's no such thing, apparently, from where it's lying.
You can't look away from a fire.
Nobody taught you to watch it this closely.
What's it doing to hold you like that?
The moon tonight.
Everyone who has ever lived looked at some version of this same moon.
You're doing the same thing they did.
A dog asleep, paws twitching.
It's running somewhere, right now, that doesn't exist.
Yours does that too, most nights.
Leaves turn color in autumn.
Nothing decided to do that.
It just happens, on schedule, without a planner.
A spider builds a web overnight — precise, load-bearing, entirely unlearned.
No one showed it how.
Where did the knowing come from?
The water you drank this morning.
By tonight some of it is sweat, some of it tears, if you cry.
Track it. When does water become you?
A tree breathed out the oxygen in your last breath.
It's a thought in your head now.
How long did that take?
Sunlight hits a leaf, becomes a plant, becomes a meal, becomes you.
You are, in part, arranged sunlight.
Sit with that a moment.
The skin on your hand right now isn't the skin you had a few weeks ago.
It was quietly replaced.
You still call it your hand.
Two people share a meal from one dish.
Months from now, some of that meal is one of you, some the other.
Where did the meal's boundary go?
The calcium in your bones was once rock, or shell, or ocean floor.
It's been many things before this.
It'll be something else after.
In a small room with other people, you're breathing air someone else just exhaled.
Their air. Now yours.
When did the switch happen?
A cut heals.
The new skin is built from what you ate that week.
Yesterday's lunch is holding you together right now.
Hold someone's hand. Warmth moves from theirs into yours.
For a moment it's hard to say whose warmth it is.
Does it matter?
Most of the water in your body was, at some point, ocean, or rain, or someone's tears.
It's on loan.
It'll move on again.
Try to find the exact moment you fell asleep last night.
You can't.
Nobody's ever caught it happening.
A vivid dream, gone completely within a minute of waking.
It felt more real than most of your day.
Where did it go?
You wake up seconds before the alarm goes off.
Nobody checked the clock for you.
What woke you?
You talk in your sleep.
Whoever was asleep wasn't deciding the words.
Who was talking?
In a dream, something happens that surprises you.
You made the whole dream.
How did you surprise yourself with your own creation?
A falling sensation jolts you awake.
The jolt happens before any thought about falling does.
What caught you?
You wake up in an unfamiliar place.
For one second, no name, no story, nowhere.
Then it all reassembles.
What was there in that one second?
A dream that returns, again, in roughly the same shape.
Different details, same architecture.
Who keeps building it?
Someone sleepwalks — moving, navigating a hallway, eyes open.
No one seems to be driving.
Who usually is?
You had plans for tonight.
Tiredness overtakes them anyway, on its own schedule.
It didn't ask permission.
A short nap, and your whole mood resets.
Nothing about the day's problems was actually solved.
What changed, then?
You try to remember a dream.
The harder you reach, the faster it dissolves.
What kind of thing disappears when you try to hold it?
You stare at a clock, willing the minute to pass.
It takes exactly as long either way.
So what were you doing?
An hour with someone you love passes like ten minutes.
The clock didn't move any differently.
Something else did.
Ten minutes in a dentist's chair feels like an hour.
Same clock as the one above.
What's actually stretching and shrinking?
Watching water almost boil, it takes forever.
Turn away for a minute, and it's already boiling.
The water didn't know you were watching.
A year goes by that felt like a handful of weeks.
Where did the rest of it go?
Not a trick question. Actually look.
A microwave counts down. You watch the seconds, impatient.
The waiting is the only thing making it feel long.
The seconds themselves don't care.
A long line at a counter.
Five minutes feels enormous.
What's actually being measured — the time, or the resistance to it?
Absorbed in something you love, hours vanish without you noticing.
Nobody was watching the clock.
Who usually is?
The clock and you are in the exact same moment right now.
It reads it as a number.
You read it as something else entirely. What?
You're impatient for something to be over.
Notice: it's only ever this moment, waiting.
There's no other moment it could be.
Walk across the room.
You didn't calculate each muscle.
Something else handled it entirely.
You trip, slightly. Your body catches your balance.
That happened before any thought about falling arrived.
What caught you?
Dancing with no one watching.
